Andaru.note: Brother native peoples of Throne (friendly with each other, raid colonizing powers from time to time); wired into Krator's fungal goods, Ranj, and volcanic sulfur networks.

Beast Riders.note: Includes the wide-ranging Millipede Tribe, which never leaves the inner crater; zero independent shipping — relies on Kautoa as its coastal presence and effective navy.

Coyote Kingdom.note: Participates in external trade while conducting frontier or desert raids that raise escort costs and shift cargo flows.

Dam Basin Salvagers.note: Boatmurder salvagers & highwaymen preying on caravans along the NE Dam Basin and semi-arid highways.

Empire of Iziz.note: Iziz modeled at 120,000 economic population; at war with Vothic Kingdom (mutual port closure, Ring Sea commerce raids outside Port Mira's 100-kil truce zone, wartime smuggling via Port Mira, Nephtos & Dhelv landing preferentially at smuggler-friendly Marr); cool relations with Kautoa; hostile to Beast Riders.

Eternal State.note: Fulcrum modeled at 120,000 economic population; mid-quality State highways link Sheritu, Mirabilis, Veil, Tone, Lux, and Farport to Fulcrum; Farport's Factory Quarter monopolizes exterior pelagic trade with The Crook (frost-coral) and Ria Valley (ria-amber).

Fellgangs.note: Participates in external trade while conducting frontier or desert raids that raise escort costs and shift cargo flows.

Free Giants (Vrivolci).note: Participates in external trade while conducting frontier or desert raids that raise escort costs and shift cargo flows.

Frogmen.note: SW Highlands native Frogmen (Krrmt & Jrrmiah); raid neighboring marches EXCEPT Realm of Dalab, with whom they maintain a peace treaty via Span.

Hookfleet.note: Port Mira on SE Throne is a major Ranj (isle-spice) supplier AND a pirate + smuggler haven accepting all ships under one strict rule: zero shipjacking within 100 Izani kils (~100 km) of the city.

Jabal Shiekdom.note: Independent Dasri oasis sheikhdom in the eastern Bowl (Jabal & Bowl Salt Works); major exporter of salt, saltpeter, pack camels/mounts, myrrh incense, and tamarisk-manna sugar.

Kautoa.note: Serves as effective navy, master shipwright, and coastal factor for the inner-crater Beast Riders; cool relations with Iziz as a result, and increasingly hostile to the Hykkousoi League (especially Tethys) over Nephtos's island claim.

Kimr.note: Semi-nomadic Pleistocene megafauna hunters gathered round the inhabited ruin of Hall of Heroes in the Labyrinth; primary exporter of mammoth/pachyderm ivory, horn, and heavy hides via dirt trails.

League: Tethys.note: Includes Nephtos (smuggling, NOT piracy haven & master shipyard colony) founded on an island claimed by Kautoa, driving severe hostility with Kautoa.

League: Ys.note: Leading Hykkousoi maritime polis; Throne colony Ybera is a major Ranj (isle-spice) plantation supplier.

Lizardmen.note: Trades strictly internally among Sauropolis, Komodo, Gila, and Tuatara; hostile to humans — zero external trade, and raids Vale of Xanadu and southern Dalab/Fellgangs.

Nomad Country.note: Participates in external trade while conducting frontier or desert raids that raise escort costs and shift cargo flows.

Painted Men.note: Participates in external trade while conducting frontier or desert raids that raise escort costs and shift cargo flows.

Ria Valley.note: Abstract exterior region whose trade arrives exclusively by ship at Farport (exporting ria-amber / frost-coral) while drawing gold, silver, and Krator's unique regional resources.

Ring Sea Pirates.note: Maritime freebooters operating out of Noa's Regret, Shanty (East Ring Isles), and Boiling Bay (Steampits), intercepting Ring Sea shipping outside Port Mira's 100-kil truce zone.

Screamer Country.note: Screamer raiders (Hexahedron) do not trade externally — raid passing caravans and neighboring marches for supplies and captives; zero external exports or imports.

Scyvoi.note: Participates in external trade while conducting frontier or desert raids that raise escort costs and shift cargo flows.

Shell Province.note: Iziz modeled at 120,000 economic population; at war with Vothic Kingdom (mutual port closure, Ring Sea commerce raids outside Port Mira's 100-kil truce zone, wartime smuggling via Port Mira, Nephtos & Dhelv landing preferentially at smuggler-friendly Marr); cool relations with Kautoa; hostile to Beast Riders.

Silkhead (Korona Gateway).note: Independent gateway town at the foot of the Korona Silk River assembling wild silk, cordage, orchil dyes, and snow-lotus reagents.

Tabisti: Liikofi.note: Independent East Abyss Tabisti city-state (no arcology in the East Abyss — zero scrap exports); exports Carboniferous swamp-copal incense, unique East Abyss lac & swamp-amber (abyss-lac), saltpeter, reed cordage, cotton, and coal.

Tabisti: Sfenops.note: Independent East Abyss Tabisti city-state (no arcology in the East Abyss — zero scrap exports); exports Carboniferous swamp-copal incense, unique East Abyss lac & swamp-amber (abyss-lac), saltpeter, reed cordage, cotton, and coal.

The Crook.note: Abstract exterior region whose trade arrives exclusively by ship at Farport (exporting ria-amber / frost-coral) while drawing gold, silver, and Krator's unique regional resources.

Tiguantin.note: Iziz tributary polity on the Eastern Highlands & Lesser Throne centered at town Guari (1095, 911); exports cushion-wool AND separate parasitic caterpillar-fungus medicine (wormwick), plus fumarole sulfur and First Monastery relics.

Vothic Kingdom.note: At war with Empire of Iziz & Shell Province; SW Bay maritime & Lake Shim river-barge trade routed through Shim (Riv 0, 5,744 m³/s) rather than inland Sethas; commercial rival of Hykkousoi League.

Yeti Kingdom.note: Raids the Eternal State (zero direct bilateral trade with Eternia); exports upland qiviut, lung-salt, birch-tar, silver, and plundered Eternian raid booty (porcelain, relics, silk, pelagic luxuries) east along the hazardous navigable Qoold Lheek–Leng–Jimjam dirt road.

Zeijani.note: Brother native peoples of Throne (friendly with each other, raid colonizing powers from time to time); wired into Krator's fungal goods, Ranj, and volcanic sulfur networks.
